avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets, money-changer touts and taxi scams around the Gongbei border crossing, especially at night.

hood_desc: A bustling border district next to the Macau crossing, dense with shops, the underground market, hotels and restaurants; suits shoppers and travelers heading to or from Macau wanting the liveliest area.
Zhuhai's central urban and administrative district, the main downtown with waterfront, malls and the Fisher Girl statue; suits first-time visitors wanting the city's core conveniences.
A coastal district with the Lovers Road promenade, seaside parks, cafes and mid-to-upscale hotels; suits travelers wanting sea views and a pleasant, walkable base.
A northern university and tech district with a preserved old town, quieter and greener; suits longer-stay visitors, students and those wanting a calmer local setting.

A rapidly developing island district next to Macau with Chimelong Ocean Kingdom, new business zones and resorts; suits families visiting the theme parks and business travelers to the new development zone.
lodging: Campanile Hotel Zhuhai Xiangzhou Yinhua Road

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or boiled water, even for brushing teeth.

transit.pay: Zhuhai has no metro yet; pay bus fares (flat ~¥2, ~$0.30) with exact cash, a Lingnan Tong regional transit card, or by scanning Alipay/WeChat Pay QR codes, which most visitors find easiest. Intercity train and ferry tickets are bought at station counters, kiosks or via the 12306/ferry operator apps.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am-10:30pm; intercity trains operate about 6:30am-10:30pm; ferries run several scheduled daily departures with no overnight service.
transit.note: A planned metro extension is still under construction and not yet open; buses, the intercity train, and cross-border ferries to Hong Kong/Macau are the practical options for now.

transit.m: Airport express bus Line 1 to downtown, ~60 min
Intercity railway to Xiangzhou station, ~50 min

landmarks: Fisher Girl Statue

This graceful bronze statue rising from the waters of Xianglu Bay has become Zhuhai's unofficial emblem, symbolizing the city's fishing heritage. It's the classic sunset photo spot along the Xiangzhou waterfront.
Zhuhai Grand Theatre (Sun and Moon Shells)

Perched dramatically on Huangyu Bay's rocky shoreline, these two shell-shaped structures glisten like giant pearls washed ashore. It's one of China's most striking pieces of contemporary architecture, especially stunning when lit up at night.
Chimelong Ocean Kingdom

One of the world's largest marine theme parks, packed with whale sharks, thrill rides, and dazzling night shows on Hengqin Island. A must for families and anyone chasing a record-breaking rollercoaster.
Lovers' Road (Qingluan Road)
This scenic coastal boulevard hugs Zhuhai's shoreline for kilometers, lined with palm trees, sculptures, and sea views toward Macau. It's beloved for cycling, jogging, and romantic evening strolls.
Qi'ao Island Mangrove Wetland

A tranquil escape from the city, this protected mangrove forest is threaded with boardwalks perfect for birdwatching and peaceful nature photography. The mudflats come alive with fiddler crabs and herons at low tide.
New Yuanmingyuan (Yuanmingxin Yuan)

A recreation of Beijing's famed Old Summer Palace, this sprawling garden complex features ornate pavilions, arched bridges, and lantern-lit nights during festivals. It's a colorful nod to classical Chinese imperial architecture.
Gongbei Port of Entry
One of the busiest border crossings on earth, this bustling gateway links Zhuhai directly to Macau. The plaza and surrounding Gongbei Underground Mall buzz with cross-border energy day and night.
Jida Fisherman's Wharf
A lively waterfront promenade of cafes, bars, and seafood restaurants with a picture-postcard view back toward the Fisher Girl statue and bay. It's the go-to spot for a relaxed evening by the water.
Dong'ao Island

Zhuhai's most beautiful outlying island offers pristine beaches, hiking trails, and a historic lighthouse with panoramic sea views. It's a favorite weekend getaway for those craving sand and clear water.
Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge Viewpoint

This engineering marvel—the world's longest sea-crossing bridge—can be admired from Zhuhai's coast, an awe-inspiring ribbon of concrete stretching across the Pearl River Delta. It's a testament to modern infrastructure ambition.

train.note: There are no cross-border trains. Zhuhai railway station sits right beside the Gongbei border checkpoint - high-speed and intercity trains run to Guangzhou and across China (book on 12306 with your passport). To reach neighbouring Macau you simply walk across the Gongbei / Portas do Cerco land border.

intl.to: Hong Kong & Macau (via the HZMB bridge)

bus.note: Cross-border coaches leave from the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge (HZMB) Zhuhai Port; the 24-hour 'Golden Bus' shuttle crosses the bridge to Hong Kong and Macau. Bring your passport and any required permits for immigration at the port.

intl.to: Hong Kong (China Ferry Terminal / airport SkyPier) - departs Jiuzhou Port

ferry.note: Ferries sail from Jiuzhou Port. Chu Kong Passenger Transport runs boats to Hong Kong in about 70 minutes (passport required), and frequent domestic ferries cross to Shenzhen's Shekou Port. Cross-border ferry frequencies have been cut since the HZMB bridge opened, so check current sailings before relying on them.
